# Labs {.unnumbered}

The Computer Lab (Slot FL, 1 credit, 0-0-2) runs for two hours each week:

| Branch | Day | Time | Room |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electrical | Tuesday | 2:00–4:00 pm | Lab 4022 |
| Mechanical | Wednesday | 2:00–4:00 pm | Lab 4022 |
| Metallurgy & Materials | Wednesday | 2:00–4:00 pm | Lab 4021 |

Bring your laptop if you have one. You can also work in the browser with [OnlineGDB](https://www.onlinegdb.com/online_c_compiler) — no installation needed. We will show you how to set up a local C toolchain (gcc/clang) in the first lab.

**Evaluation:** regular lab work counts for **20%** of the course grade (see [Assessment](./course.qmd#assessment)). Lab 1 is a setup session and is not graded; every lab from Lab 2 onwards is evaluated with equal weight.

## Lab Schedule

The schedule below is **tentative** and covers all 11 practical modules of the [syllabus](./syllabus.qmd) (the *module* column refers to the syllabus practical table). Lab handouts are **self-contained**: where a lab reaches a construct before its full lecture treatment, the handout introduces just enough of it to do the exercises. Because institute holidays fall on different weekdays, the Tuesday (EE) and Wednesday (Mech/Materials) batches drift by a week in places — go by the *session number*, not the date.

| # | EE (Tue) | Mech & Materials (Wed) | Topic | Module |
|:---:|---|---|---|:---:|
| [1](labsheets/lab01.qmd) | Aug 4 | Aug 5 | Basic input/output programs (incl. toolchain & editor setup) | 1 |
| [2](labsheets/lab02.qmd) | Aug 18 | Aug 19 | First C programs: printf/scanf, variables, operators — graded set e1–e5 | 1 |
| [3](labsheets/lab03.qmd) | Aug 25 | Sep 2 | **Solid ground** — consolidation: types, operators, precedence, integer vs. real division | 1 |
| [4](labsheets/lab04.qmd) | Sep 1 | Sep 9 | Loops: `for`, `while` and `do-while`, and converting between them | 5, 6 |
| [5](labsheets/lab05.qmd) | Sep 8 | Sep 16 | Lists and strings: arrays, strings as character arrays | 3 |
| [6](labsheets/lab06.qmd) | Sep 15 | Sep 30 | Using libraries (`string.h`, `math.h`, etc.) | 10 |
| [7](labsheets/lab07.qmd) | Sep 29 | Oct 7 | Functions and recursion | 7 |
| [8](labsheets/lab08.qmd) | Oct 6 | Oct 14 | Tuples & dictionaries, C-style: structures and key–value lookup tables | 4 |
| [9](labsheets/lab09.qmd) | Oct 13 | Oct 21 | File handling | 8 |
| [10](labsheets/lab10.qmd) | Oct 27 | Oct 28 | Error handling | 9 |
| [11](labsheets/lab11.qmd) | Nov 3 | Nov 4 | Problem solving I (GATE / ACM ICPC style) | 11 |
| [12](labsheets/lab12.qmd) | Nov 17 | Nov 18 | Problem solving II | 11 |

: {tbl-colwidths="[6,13,20,53,8]"}

**No lab on:** Wed Aug 26 (Milad-un-Nabi), Tue Sep 22 & Wed Sep 23 (mid-semester exams), Tue Oct 20 (Dussehra), Tue Nov 10 & Wed Nov 11 (holidays).

::: {.callout-note}
The syllabus allocates 28 practical hours (8 of them for problem solving); holidays leave **12 sessions = 24 hours**. Two adjustments close the gap: modules 5 and 6 are taught together in Lab 4 (`for`, `while` and `do-while` are one idea in three costumes, and converting between them is a better exercise than meeting them a week apart), and the remaining problem-solving hours are covered through a make-up lab session (date TBA) plus problems embedded in earlier sheets — Lab 3 alone carries 24 practice problems.
:::

## Lab Manual (reference)

The department's shared lab manual for this course covers the ground every section works
from, and several lab sheets and lecture decks refer to it by section number:

| Manual | Sections worth bookmarking |
|---|---|
| 📕 [**The C Programming Laboratory**](labs/CLab3_Aroof.pdf) (PDF, 12 pp.) | **§1** the `vim` editor · **§2.5** the C compilation model (preprocessor → compiler → assembler → linker) · **§2.7–2.8** variables, types, `#define` vs `const`, escape sequences · **§2.9–2.10** operators and the full **precedence table** · **§3** `printf` and `scanf` |

: {tbl-colwidths="[28,72]"}

*Prepared by [Aroof Aimen](https://www.iitjammu.ac.in/faculty/~aroofaimen), Department of
Computer Science & Engineering, IIT Jammu — Laboratory Manual Part II, August 2026. Shared
across all sections of CS-1-01 (MO); reproduced here with thanks.*

## Useful Tools

- [OnlineGDB C compiler](https://www.onlinegdb.com/online_c_compiler) — write, run, and debug in the browser.
- [C Tutor (pythontutor.com)](https://pythontutor.com/c.html) — visualize the step-by-step execution of C programs.
- [Search & sort visualizations](https://www.cs.usfca.edu/~galles/visualization/Search.html) — see linear vs. binary search in action.
- MIT OCW 6.087 [labs and assignments](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-087-practical-programming-in-c-january-iap-2010/pages/assignments/) — extra practice problems with solutions.
